### 1. The constraint that deferred this card on 2026-09-07 is GONE

Comment `5571981718` deferred it because `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts` was held by in-flight #15617. Measured now:

- **#15617 is `closed` / `completed`**, unassigned.
- Across all **22 open PRs** in this repo (enumerated at 09:20–09:22Z, each PR's file list read), **no open PR touches** `automation/execution.zod.ts`, `api/export.zod.ts`, `integration/connector.zod.ts`, `system/cache.zod.ts` or `system/disaster-recovery.zod.ts`. The five schema files this card writes are unheld.
- The card's own sequencing precondition also holds: **#15028 and #15035 are both `closed` / `completed`**, so the `shared/expression.zod.ts` narrowing this card was told to follow has landed.

### 2. The new adjacency, and why it is NOT a serial

This card must register ADR-0087 D3 entries, which lands in `packages/spec/src/migrations/`. In-flight **PR #16777** (card #14791) writes there too:

```
added    packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-react-list-view-binding-aliases-retired.ts
modified packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts
```

At first read that is a shared single-writer file. It is not — `registry.ts`'s own docblock says so:

> ## ⚠️ The three tables below are GENERATED (#7297)
> Each step's `semantic` list, `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` and `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` are concatenated into their `<os-generated …>` regions from `./entries/`, **one file per entry**, sorted by entry id. Add an entry by adding a FILE and running `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` — never by typing between the markers.

⇒ The **authored** inputs of the two cards are disjoint (a different new file each), and the only shared surface is a generated region with a defined reconciliation procedure. Under 「并行纪律」 that is parallel-eligible, not 「同文件单跨轮硬串行」.

**The obligation this creates for whoever claims this card** — carry it into the claim comment and the PR:

- ⛔ Never type between the `<os-generated …>` markers; add the entry FILE and run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry`.
- **`scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`'s four-step is mandatory before enqueue.** Two PRs regenerating one region is exactly the case it exists for: without it, a merge silently swallows the other side's regeneration and rolls its anchors back.
- Merge `main` once before opening the PR, and again after #16777 lands — then re-run the generator, not a hand-merge of the region.

### 3. Why it is still not dispatched right now

The lane is at its dispatch cap of **3 devs in flight** (#16715, #16328, #16512, all claimed 09:22Z). This card is L — seven positions across five schema files, five ADR-0087 D3 entries, tombstones plus refusal pins, regeneration of the authorable-surface shards / JSON schema / api-surface / reference pages, and retirement of the D7 `cron-declared-unwired` ledger rows. It is **next in this lane** when a slot frees; the deferral is capacity, not merit — it carries the #15954 ruling (option A per family, maintainer 「其他同意」, batch #56).

### 4. The pit to record now rather than when someone picks it up

⚠️ **The card's line-number table is anchored to `origin/main` `f1e91595f` and `origin/main` has moved to `5e53d73d8`+.** The card already says "re-locate by text" — that instruction is now load-bearing, not decorative. Every one of the seven positions must be found by its schema and field name, ⛔ never by the line number in the table.

⚠️ The connector position (`DataSyncConfig.schedule`) is the only one reachable from a stack manifest, so it is the only one whose ADR-0087 entry must state a measured author population — and the out-of-repo half of that population is **NOT MEASURABLE** from this repo. Say so in the entry rather than implying zero.

This is the non-obvious one, so the evidence is here rather than left for the claimant to rediscover:

⇒ Claim it `yes`. ⛔ Not because the direction is widening, but because the instrument that gates enqueue reads it that way and two precedents agree.

### 3 · ⭐ Only ONE of the seven is reachable from a stack manifest — the per-family split is not a style choice

`DataSyncConfig.schedule` is reachable: `stack.zod.ts:685` `connectors: z.array(DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema)` → `connector.zod.ts:955` → `:799 syncConfig: DataSyncConfigSchema.optional()`, plus the `connector` metadata door. **The other six have no consumer outside their own file and the D7 ledger** (control: `ConnectorSchema` lights five connector packages plus service-automation, so the probe is not blind).

⇒ The connector family needs the **D2 conversion** shape (`conversions/registry.ts:8406-8450`, the `connector-error-mapping-removed` precedent: `mapCollection(stack, 'connectors', …)`, `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`) **plus** the `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence. The other six take the #15514 shape: no D2, no migrate sentence.

### 4 · ⭐⭐ The predicted failure has NO GATE — this is what the dispatch order will be written against

Copying PR #15514 wholesale omits the D2 conversion for the connector family, and **nothing catches it**: gate (b) in `build-schemas.ts` checks `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` registration, not conversions, and the chain-replay test only sees a conversion that exists. The mirror error is writing the migrate sentence on **all seven** — that sentence must be true of the tool (`retired-key.ts:53-63`) and is pinned class-wide by `retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts`.

### 5 · ⚠️ This card reaches a PUBLISHED, GOVERNED surface the body does not name

`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md:426` lists `connector.schedule`, `automation/execution.cronExpression` and `api/export.cronExpression` as cron carriers (control: `Job.schedule` hits one file). A spec-only PR therefore leaves a **published skill teaching three retired carriers**, and reds only in CI. Touching it makes the PR **governed** — draft-only, human merge, and a PM-set net-line budget in the dispatch order. Also carrying stale text: `packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md:51,:99,:194` and `@example` blocks at `export.zod.ts:562`, `disaster-recovery.zod.ts:19,:204`.
